Intake Note - 09/26/2026

Problem: Water leaking through the bathroom ceiling for 8 weeks.

History: Tenant reports a progressive ceil-
ing leak in the bathroom with mold spreading over the wall
behind the toilet. The leak began after a storm on 08/01/2026.

Notice given: Sent 6 weeks of written notice to the landlord
(3 letters) and called the management office twice a week, with
“no response.”

Inspection: Active drip from the bathroom ceiling light fixture.
Black mold over 4 square feet of the wall (photo 4/5). Floor
dry. No signiﬁcant damage to other rooms.

Emergencies: None. No gas leak, no sewage backup, no exposed
wiring, no loss of heat.

Assessment: Habitability defect, water intrusion (HC 12.4), not
repaired after written notice.

Plan: Repair and deduct for the ceiling leak, or a demand letter
to the landlord before filing in housing court.

Electronically signed: Elena Marsh, Tenant Organizer

versions.name: policy_ip112
versions.title: Policy IP-112: Repair and deduct
versions.content:
# Northwind Legal Aid: Intake Policy IP-112

## Repair and Deduct Cases

### Criteria

We accept a tenant's repair and deduct case for full representation when any of the following criteria are met:

1. Emergency conditions, such as a gas leak, sewage backup, exposed wiring, or no heat in freezing weather.
2. A needed repair still not made after at least 6 weeks of written notice to the landlord.
3. Worsening conditions or a serious threat to health or safety.

### Definitions

Written notice includes a letter, an email, or a message through a tenant portal, sent to the landlord or the landlord's agent.

Emergency conditions include a gas leak, sewage backup, and no heat when the outside temperature is below freezing.

# Intake summary: Jordan Avery

Request: repair and deduct for a bathroom ceiling leak (HC 12.4), referred by Riverside Tenants Union.

## Findings

- Water leaking through the bathroom ceiling for 8 weeks.
- The tenant reports a "progressive ceiling leak in the bathroom" with mold spreading over the wall behind the toilet.
- Active drip from the bathroom ceiling light fixture.
- No significant damage to other rooms.

## Criteria check

| Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Repair not made | Habitability defect, water intrusion (HC 12.4) |
| At least 6 weeks of written notice | Six weeks of letters and calls, with no response |
| No emergency | No gas leak, no sewage backup, no exposed wiring, no loss of heat. |

Policy IP-112 accepts a case when a needed repair is still not made after at least 6 weeks of written notice, and letters and emails both count as written notice.
